faqs.a:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning:
Environmental site assessment (assessment)
shall mean an evaluation of the environmental condition of property consisting of
               the following three phases:
(1)
Phase I assessment.
This phase shall consist of those physical examinations, test, and review of historical
                  ownership of the property as are reasonable and prudent in determining the likelihood
                  that there exists on the property any hazardous substances; the city may promulgate
                  regulations detailing with specificity the examinations, tests, and sources of information
                  which must be researched as a part of this phase; this phase shall culminate in a
                  written report of findings including a recommendation regarding whether a Phase II
                  assessment is necessary.
(2)
Phase II assessment.
This phase shall at a minimum consist of a physical examination of the property,
                  and adjacent property if feasible, including an examination of any facilities, processes
                  and practices thereon; such physical examination shall include any tests and samplings
                  of soil, water, air, vegetation, facilities and/or any improvements whatsoever as
                  required by the city as a result of information provided in the Phase I assessment
                  in order to determine the presence or absence of hazardous substances on the property;
                  the city may promulgate regulations detailing with specificity the nature of testing
                  and sampling required for Phase II assessments; this phase shall culminate in a written
                  report of findings regarding any testing and sampling results as well as a recommendation
                  regarding whether any remediation is necessary, and, if so, a description thereof;
                  reporting shall be subject to compliance with federal, state and local regulations
                  or requirements.
(3)
Phase III assessment.
This phase shall consist of remediation of hazardous substances on the property as
                  recommended by a Phase II assessment, subject to compliance with federal, state or
                  local regulations or requirements.
Hazardous substance
means any substance, material, waste, or mixture designated as a hazardous material,
               waste, or substance according to 49 CFR 172, as amended, or by C.R.S. § 18-13-112(2)(b),
               or by C.R.S. § 25-15-101(6)(a), or as designated pursuant to the Federal "Comprehensive
               Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act of 1980" (CERCLA), as amended
               by the Superfund Amendments and Reauthorization Act of 1986 (SARA), 42 USC 9601-75,
               and further, shall mean and include, without limitation, any flammable materials,
               explosive, hazardous or toxic substances or related materials as defined and hereafter
               amended in 42 USC 9601-14; and "chemical substances" as defined and hereafter amended
               in 15 USC 2602-2; and "hazardous waste" as defined and hereafter amended in 42 USC
               6903-5; and "petroleum" as defined and hereafter amended in 42 USC 6991-8; and "hazardous
               materials" as defined and hereafter amended in 49 USC 1802-2. The term "hazardous
               substances" as defined herein shall apply to any and all such substances in connection
               with any property to which this article applies, regardless of whether such substances
               are located under the ground, on the ground, in water, in the air, in buildings or
               other enclosures, or in any containers whatsoever. Wherever a more stringent or less
               stringent interpretation of the definition of "hazardous substance" is possible, the
               more stringent interpretation shall be applied.
Property
shall mean any real property including any buildings or structures or improvements
               located thereon.
Property owner
or
owner
shall mean the owner or titleholder of any fee, leasehold, or possessory interest
               in property subject to the requirements herein and shall include the singular or plural,
               as appropriate, and shall include any agent, representative, person or entity authorized
               by the property owner to act on his behalf.
Public entity
shall mean United States government including any department, agency, or bureau thereof;
               the state and any political subdivision thereof; or any county, school district, special
               district, quasi-municipal corporation, or urban renewal authority.
Remediation
shall mean the action or measures taken, or to be taken, by the city or the property
               owner, whether directly by owner or by the city, or through a contractor or agent
               of owner or city, which purpose is to lessen, clean-up, remove, ameliorate, dispose
               of, vitiate, or mitigate the existence of hazardous substances existing on the property
               to such standards, specifications, or requirements as may be established or required
               by the Environmental Protection Agency, the Colorado Department of Public Health and
               Environment, or any authorized local agency or city department. This definition shall
               apply to the past, present and future tenses of the word "remediation."
(Code 1981, § 25-83; Ord. No. 3009, § 1, 10-4-1993)
